spots.name: San Diego Zoo
spots.summary: The San Diego Zoo is a zoo in San Diego, California, United States, located in Balboa Park. It began with a collection of animals left over from the 1915 Panama–California Exposition that were brought together by its founder, Harry M. Wegeforth.

spots.name: Balboa Park
spots.summary: Balboa Park is a 1,200-acre (490 ha) historic urban cultural park in San Diego, California. Placed in reserve in 1835, the park's site is one of the oldest in the United States dedicated to public recreational use. The park hosts various museums, theaters, restaurants, and the San Diego Zoo.

spots.name: Hotel del Coronado
spots.summary: The Hotel del Coronado, also known as The Del and Hotel Del, is a historic beachfront hotel in Coronado, California, just across San Diego Bay from San Diego.

spots.name: USS Midway Museum
spots.summary: The USS Midway Museum is a historical naval aircraft carrier museum in San Diego, California, United States, located at Navy Pier. The museum consists of the aircraft carrier Midway. The ship houses an extensive collection of aircraft, many of which were built in Southern California.

spots.name: Santa Fe Depot
spots.summary: Santa Fe Depot is a union station in San Diego, California, built by the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway to replace the small Victorian-style structure erected in 1887 for the California Southern Railroad Company.

spots.name: Star of India
spots.summary: Star of India is an iron-hulled sailing ship, built in 1863 in Ramsey, Isle of Man, as the full-rigged ship Euterpe. After a career sailing from Great Britain to India and New Zealand, she was renamed, re-rigged as a barque, and became a salmon hauler on the Alaska to California route.

names.ja: スター・オブ・インディア

spots.name: San Diego–Coronado Bridge
spots.summary: The San Diego–Coronado Bridge, commonly referred to as the Coronado Bridge, is a prestressed concrete/steel girder fixed-link bridge crossing over San Diego Bay, linking San Diego with Coronado, California. It is signed as part of State Route 75.

photo.author: U.S. Navy photo by Photographer's Mate 2nd Class Larry S. Carlson

spots.name: San Diego Museum of Art

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: The San Diego Museum of Art is a fine art museum in Balboa Park in San Diego, California, that houses a broad collection with particular strength in Spanish art. It opened as the Fine Arts Gallery of San Diego on February 28, 1926, and changed to its current name in 1978.

names.es: Museo de Arte de San Diego

spots.name: Horton Plaza Park
spots.summary: Horton Plaza Park is an outdoor plaza in downtown San Diego, California. It includes an amphitheater, retail stores, and a fountain. It is located on the corner of 4th Avenue and Broadway.

spots.name: Timken Museum of Art

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Timken Museum of Art is a fine art museum in Balboa Park in San Diego, California, close to the San Diego Museum of Art. It was established in 1965.

spots.name: Museum of Us
spots.summary: The Museum of Us is a museum of anthropology located in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. The museum is housed in the historic landmark buildings of the California Quadrangle.

names.fr: Musée de l'Homme de San Diego
names.es: Museo del Hombre de San Diego

spots.name: One America Plaza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One America Plaza is the tallest building in San Diego, California, and a prominent fixture in the waterfront district of the downtown San Diego skyline. The 34-story, 500 ft (150 m), 623,000 sq ft (57,900 m2), obelisk-shaped tower was designed by Helmut Jahn of Murphy/Jahn Architects and KMA Architecture.

spots.name: San Diego Air & Space Museum
spots.summary: The San Diego Air & Space Museum (SDASM) is an aviation and space exploration museum in San Diego, California. It is located in Balboa Park and is housed in the former Ford Building, which is listed on the US National Register of Historic Places.

names.fr: Musée de l'air et de l'espace de San Diego
names.ja: サンディエゴ航空宇宙博物館
names.zh: 圣迭戈航空航天博物馆

spots.name: Pechanga Arena
spots.summary: Pechanga Arena is an indoor arena in San Diego, California. Opened in 1966, it is an example of New Formalism architecture and has been designated by the City of San Diego as a historic resource. The arena has been home to numerous athletic teams in various sports.

names.ja: サンディエゴ・スポーツセンター

spots.name: Whaley House
spots.summary: The Whaley House is a Greek Revival–style residence and museum in Old Town, San Diego, California. It is the oldest brick structure in Southern California, built in 1857. It is a California Historical Landmark No. 65 and is currently maintained by Historic Tours of America, Inc (HTA).

spots.name: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park
spots.summary: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park is a state protected historical park in the Old Town neighborhood of San Diego, California. The park commemorates the early days of San Diego; it includes many historic buildings from the period 1820 to 1870. The park was established in 1968.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Old Town San Diego State Historic Park

names.fr: Parc historique d'État d'Old Town San Diego
names.es: Old Town San Diego State Park

spots.name: Journey to Atlantis
spots.summary: Journey to Atlantis is the name shared by three water roller coasters located at SeaWorld amusement parks. These attractions, while different in layout and statistics from one another, tell similar stories of a trip to the mythical land of Atlantis.

spots.name: Harbor Club Condominiums

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Harbor Club Condominiums is a high-rise residential building in San Diego, California, United States, composed of two towers of equal height. The 41-story towers have a height of 424 feet (129 m) and are a prominent fixture in the city's skyline.

spots.name: Tower 180

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Tower 180, formerly the Executive Complex, is a 25-story building located at 180 Broadway in San Diego, California, United States. Upon completion in 1963, the 106.68 m (350.0 ft) building was the tallest in the city until 1969.

spots.name: San Diego Natural History Museum
spots.summary: The San Diego Natural History Museum is a museum in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It was founded in 1874 as the San Diego Society of Natural History. It is the second oldest scientific institution west of the Mississippi and the oldest in Southern California.

names.es: Museo de Historia Natural de San Diego
names.ja: サンディエゴ自然史博物館
names.zh: 圣地亚哥自然史博物馆

spots.name: Old Globe Theatre
spots.summary: The Old Globe is a professional theatre company in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It produces about 15 plays and musicals annually in summer and winter seasons.

names.ja: オールド・グローブ・シアター

spots.name: Chicano Park
spots.summary: Chicano Park is a 7.9 acres (32,000 m2) park in Barrio Logan, a predominantly Chicano/Mexican American community in central San Diego, California.

spots.name: Mingei International Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Mingei International Museum is a non-profit public institution in Balboa Park in San Diego, California, that collects, conserves and exhibits folk art, craft, and design. The museum was founded in 1974, and its building opened in 1978. The word mingei, meaning 'art of the people,' was coined by the Japanese scholar Dr.

spots.name: Presidio of San Diego
spots.summary: El Presidio Real de San Diego is a historic fort in San Diego, California. It was established on May 14, 1769, by Gaspar de Portolá, leader of the first European land exploration of Alta California—at that time an unexplored northwestern frontier area of New Spain.

spots.name: Hilton San Diego Bayfront

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hilton San Diego Bayfront is a hotel in San Diego, California. The 30-story structure is 385 ft-tall (117 m), containing 1,190 suites.

spots.name: California Quadrangle
spots.summary: The California Quadrangle, California Building, and California Tower are historic structures located in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. They were built for the 1915–16 Panama–California Exposition and served as the grand entry to the event. The buildings and courtyard were designed by architect Bertram Goodhue.

spots.name: Maritime Museum of San Diego
spots.summary: The Maritime Museum of San Diego is a maritime museum in San Diego, California. Established in 1948, it preserves one of the largest collections of historic sea vessels in the United States. Located on San Diego Bay, the centerpiece of the museum's collection is Star of India, an 1863 iron barque.

names.ja: サンディエゴ海洋博物館

spots.name: San Diego Model Railroad Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The San Diego Model Railroad Museum is a museum in San Diego, California, that focuses on the heritage of railroading through model railroads. It was founded in 1982. The museum is located on the lower level of Casa de Balboa in Balboa Park.

spots.name: Museum of Photographic Arts

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu

spots.summary: The Museum of Photographic Arts (MOPA) is a museum in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. First founded in 1974, MOPA opened in 1983.

spots.name: Fleet Science Center
spots.summary: The Fleet Science Center is a science museum and planetarium in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. Established in 1973, it was the first science museum to combine interactive science exhibits with a planetarium and an IMAX Dome (OMNIMAX) theater, setting the standard that most major science museums follow today.

names.fr: Reuben H. Fleet Space Theater and Science Center
names.es: Centro de Ciencias Reuben H. Fleet

spots.name: Cabrillo Bridge
spots.summary: The Cabrillo Bridge is a historic bridge in San Diego, California, providing pedestrian and light automotive access between Balboa Park and the uptown area of San Diego. It was built for the Panama–California Exposition of 1915.

spots.name: St. Joseph Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Joseph Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral in the Cortez Hill neighborhood of San Diego, California, in the United States. It is the seat of the Diocese of San Diego.

names.es: Catedral de San José de San Diego

spots.name: Petco Park
spots.summary: Petco Park is a ballpark in San Diego, California. It is the home of the San Diego Padres of Major League Baseball (MLB). The ballpark is located in the East Village neighborhood of downtown San Diego, adjacent to the Gaslamp Quarter.

spots.name: Berkeley
spots.summary: Berkeley was one of several ferryboats of the Southern Pacific Railroad that for sixty years operated on San Francisco Bay between the Oakland Pier and the San Francisco Ferry Building.

spots.name: Spreckels Organ Pavilion
spots.summary: The Spreckels Organ Pavilion is an outdoor venue that houses the open-air Spreckels Organ in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. With more than 5,000 pipes, the Spreckels Organ is the world's largest pipe organ in a fully outdoor venue.

spots.name: Symphony Towers

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Symphony Towers is a 1.2-million-square-foot late modernist two-tower hotel and office complex in San Diego, California, located in the historic Financial District of downtown San Diego.

spots.name: House of Charm

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The House of Charm is a historic museum building in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It was built for the 1915–16 Panama–California Exposition, and like most buildings from the exposition, it features Mission Revival architecture. It acquired its current name during the California Pacific International Exposition.

spots.name: Statue of Alonzo Horton
spots.summary: Alonzo E. Horton is a statue of the American real estate developer Alonzo Horton, installed at the intersection of Third Avenue and E Street, in San Diego, California.

spots.name: San Diego History Center
spots.summary: The San Diego History Center is a museum in Balboa Park in San Diego, California, dedicated to the history of San Diego.

spots.name: Statue of Ernest W. Hahn
spots.summary: Ernest W. Hahn is a sculpture of the founder of shopping center developer Hahn Company, installed outside San Diego's Horton Plaza Park, in the U.S. state of California.

spots.name: San Diego County Administration Center
spots.summary: The San Diego County Administration Center is a historic Beaux-Arts/Spanish Revival–style building in San Diego, California. It houses the offices of the government of San Diego County. Due to its notable architecture and location fronting San Diego Bay, it is nicknamed the Jewel on the Bay.

spots.name: Comic-Con Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Comic-Con Museum is an art museum in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. The museum focuses on comics and related popular arts through exhibits, programs, and events drawn from San Diego Comic-Con.

spots.name: San Diego Art Institute

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The San Diego Art Institute was a contemporary art museum with a focus on artists from the Southern California and Baja Norte region. It was founded in 1941 as the San Diego Business Men's Art Club. Its name was changed in 1950 to the San Diego Art Institute. In 1953, women were admitted for membership.

names.es: Instituto de Arte de San Diego

spots.name: Gallagher Square
spots.summary: Gallagher Square is a 2.8-acre (1.1 ha) park located outside the outfield fence of Petco Park in San Diego, California. It is a public park during stadium off-hours, it includes a viewing terrace, playground, and off-leash dog park.

spots.name: Japanese Friendship Garden
spots.summary: The Japanese Friendship Garden and Museum is a Japanese garden in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It is an expression of friendship between San Diego and its sister city Yokohama.

spots.name: Zoro Garden
spots.summary: Zoro Garden is a six-acre sunken garden in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It is located between the Fleet Science Center and Casa de Balboa. The name refers to the Persian mystic Zoroaster.

spots.name: Pinnacle Marina Tower

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Pinnacle Marina Tower is a high rise building in San Diego, California, United States. It was completed in 2005 as the Pinnacle Museum Tower, and is the second tallest residential building in the city with a height of 449 feet (137 m).

spots.name: Pythias Lodge Building
spots.summary: The Pythias Lodge Building in San Diego, California, also known as Community Arts Complex or Intercultural Council of the Arts, is a Beaux Arts architecture building built in 1911.

spots.name: Nikigator
spots.summary: Nikigator is a permanent public artwork by Franco‑American sculptor Niki de Saint Phalle, installed at the entrance of the Mingei International Museum in San Diego, California.

spots.name: El Prado Complex
spots.summary: El Prado Complex is a historic district in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. The 13-acre (5.3 ha) complex includes 13 contributing buildings and one contributing structure.

spots.name: San Diego Automotive Museum
spots.summary: The San Diego Automotive Museum is a museum in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It contains a collection of cars and motorcycles illustrating the history of American automotive culture.

spots.name: San Diego Viejo Plaza
spots.summary: San Diego Viejo Plaza, also called Plaza de Las Armas, Old Town Plaza, and Washington Square, is a historical site in San Diego, California. The San Diego Viejo Plaza site is California Historical Landmark No. 63, listed on December 5, 1932.

spots.name: Starlight Bowl
spots.summary: The Starlight Bowl is an amphitheater in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It was constructed for the 1935–1936 California Pacific International Exposition and seats 4,300.

spots.name: George W. Marston House
spots.summary: The George W. Marston House is a museum and historic landmark in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It is maintained by Save Our Heritage Organisation (SOHO).

spots.name: The Rady Shell at Jacobs Park
spots.summary: The Rady Shell at Jacobs Park is an open-air music venue in San Diego, California. It first opened in 2021, and is operated by the San Diego Symphony on the grounds of Embarcadero Marina Park South, which the symphony leases from the Port of San Diego.
spots.wikipediaTitle: The Rady Shell at Jacobs Park

spots.name: Plaza de Panama
spots.summary: Plaza de Panama is a plaza in Balboa Park's El Prado Complex in San Diego, California.

spots.name: The New Children's Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The New Children's Museum is an arts–based children's museum in downtown San Diego, California, whose mission is to "stimulate imagination, creativity and critical thinking in children and families through inventive and engaging experiences with contemporary art".

spots.name: Ford Building
spots.summary: The Ford Building is a Streamline Moderne structure in Balboa Park in San Diego, California, that serves as the home of the San Diego Air & Space Museum. The building was built by the Ford Motor Company for the California Pacific International Exposition, which was held in 1935 and 1936.

spots.name: Alcazar Garden
spots.summary: Alcazar Garden is a formal garden in Balboa Park in San Diego, California. It is named for Alcazar Castle in Seville, Spain; its design is patterned after the castle's gardens.

spots.name: Harbor Drive Pedestrian Bridge
spots.summary: Harbor Drive Pedestrian Bridge is a self-anchored suspension bridge in San Diego, California. A pedestrian and bicycle crossing, it spans the San Diego Trolley and San Diego and Arizona Eastern Railway in downtown San Diego.

spots.name: Gaslamp Quarter Park
spots.summary: A small square next to the Gaslamp Quarter trolley station with a small water fountain. Good views of the convention center.

spots.name: Black Hawk Smithy & Stable
spots.summary: Established in 1860. At the site, visitors can watch blacksmithing and other demonstrations.

spots.name: Seeley Stable Museum
spots.summary: A reconstructed stage coach stop with a collection of vintage carriages inside.

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: Just north of Santa Fe Depot, this museum holds a part of the museum's collection over 4,000 works.

spots.name: San Diego Chinese Historical Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: A museum dedicated to Chinese history, culture and art. Includes exhibits on the Chinese experience in America.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A historic Mission-style church in Old Town dating back to 1919.

spots.name: Red Fox Steakhouse and Piano Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Charming place where it's easy to imagine you've time-traveled to the early 1970s. Don't expect cutting-edge cuisine, but when your parents or grandparents wanted to have a nice evening out, they probably went somewhere like this. The bar furnishings came from a 17th-century English pub - think mood lighting and lots of dark leather and oak. Also a good place for a cocktail or two. Live music nigh

spots.name: Zia Gourmet Pizza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Zias is home to some of the most unique and tastiest pizzas in all San Diego. You can order by the slice or a whole pie. The types of pizza range from the traditional cheese (three types) to the most famous, eggplant (cranberries, walnuts, yogurt, and eggplant). All food served is kosher and halal and there are vegan options as well. The owner and head chef constantly walks around and asks how eve

spots.name: Lestat's Coffee House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lestat's never closes, ever. Aside from the specialty coffee drinks and the local pastries, the walls are covered with art for sale, and the next door stage has nightly shows and open mics. Free wifi attracts all sorts of local characters and the back is always packed with people. They have a sister location in University Heights along Park Avenue.

spots.name: The Big Kitchen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This restaurant is so named because the kitchen is bigger than the rest of the restaurant. "Judy The Beauty (on Duty)" is usually there serving up great food (mainly breakfast, but also lunch), with a cheerful attitude. Take time to appreciate the bumper stickers and celebrity posters on the walls - Whoopi Goldberg once worked here.

spots.name: Blind Lady Ale House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: With a pub vibe and aesthetic, BLAH's a fantastic place to drink a wide selection of local craft brew and munch on some pizza. During the week it's not nearly as crowded--you'll be able to find a spot on the long wooden tables. If you ride your bike there, you can get a 10% discount when you show your helmet at the bar.

spots.name: Ponces Mexican Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ponces has been renovated, offering a bar and better seating but it still offers some of the best American Mexican food in San Diego. Not authentic Mexican food, but good American Mexican food. Get there with enough time to wait and if you don't want dine in call for take out.

spots.name: Cosmopolitan Restaurant and Hotel
spots.summary: A beautiful dining establishment in a building built by Juan Bandini in 1829. Later, in the 1860s, a second story was added and it became the Cosmopolitan Hotel. You can eat in the garden amid flowers, trees, and fountains or inside the wonderful historic building.

spots.name: Knotty Barrel

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sun

spots.summary: Cool gastropub with a great menu and wonderful selection of draft beers. Try a sample of four beers for $7 to see what you like. If none of the draft beers suit your taste, there's a multitude of other beers from all over the world listed on the chalkboard.

spots.name: The Mission

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Third and newest of the popular locally owned breakfast restaurant. Avoid the lines at the North Park and Mission Beach locations by coming here. Vegetarian offerings for the diet conscious. Only open for breakfast and lunch from 8AM - 3PM.

spots.name: Underbelly

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Serves tonkotsu (pork broth) and vegetarian ramen. Gets crowded, expect to wait for seating if you arrive during the lunch or dinner rush. There is also a North Park location with a slightly different menu.

spots.name: Bleu Boheme

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Charming, rustic neighborhood French brasserie in the heart of Kensington. They feature a prix fixe Bohemian menu every night from 5-6PM, all night on Tuesdays. Try the moules frites in Roquefort sauce.

spots.name: Khyber Pass
spots.summary: A mix of Afghan, Turkish, and Indian dishes served by a friendly staff. Lamb, beef, chicken, and vegetarian/vegan dishes. It'son University Avenue among many other restaurants. Street parking only.

spots.name: The Prado
spots.summary: Just about the only full-service restaurant in Balboa Park (save for a couple of places in the zoo), The Prado has a diverse menu with appetizers, salads, soups, seafood, pastas, and sandwiches.

spots.name: Mona Lisa Restaurant & Deli

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Enjoy Sicilian style favorites and some of the best pizza in town at this family-oriented restaurant. Deli has large selection of Italian imports and is a great place to grab a sandwich.

spots.name: El Dorado

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Western-themed hipster hangout with good cocktails, rotating DJs, and a fun dance floor. A world away from the usual bottleservice & bouncers experience at many downtown SD clubs.

spots.name: Fifth Avenue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This section of Fifth Ave contains many of the most popular clubs and bars in San Diego, and is typically seen as the heart of San Diego’s nightlife.

spots.name: The Field

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Irish pub literally shipped over piece by piece from Ireland and reassembled. Good food and drinks, and frequent live Irish music.

spots.name: Ballast Point

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Little Italy tasting room and gastropub for one of San Diego's best known craft brewers. Several other locations around the city.

spots.name: Kensington Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This coffee shop, loved by the locals, serves coffee, tea, food and even spumoni.

spots.name: The Wine Lover

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A lovely wine bar with a wide selection of wines and some light meals.
